q_vis.title: 1. Cost Visibility & Insight
q_vis.desc: How is Azure spend allocated, reported and distributed to the business teams?
q_vis.CRAWL: Manual review of the Azure invoice at month end. No self-service dashboards and no automated budgets.
q_vis.WALK: Budgets configured per subscription with alerts, and daily cost data export to central storage.
q_vis.RUN: Automated showback/chargeback to cost centers, with real-time unit-cost telemetry per business transaction.

q_rate.title: 2. Rate Optimization
q_rate.desc: What strategy is applied to compute commitments and hybrid licensing?
q_rate.CRAWL: Compute is 100% on demand (pay-as-you-go). No reservation analysis and no Azure Hybrid Benefit enabled.
q_rate.WALK: Reserved Instance and Savings Plan coverage above 60% on stable workloads, with Hybrid Benefit on the main VMs.
q_rate.RUN: Algorithmic commitment management (>85% coverage), Azure Spot in pipelines, and continuous rate arbitrage.

q_usage.title: 3. Usage Optimization
q_usage.desc: How is over-provisioning and idle cloud capacity managed?
q_usage.CRAWL: Over-provisioned resources are fixed only after a budget incident. VMs run 24/7 with no automatic shutdown.
q_usage.WALK: Fortnightly review of Azure Advisor recommendations, with scheduled shutdown policies in development environments.
q_usage.RUN: Elastic auto-scaling in production, event-driven serverless architecture, and automated deletion of zombie resources.

q_gov.title: 4. Governance & Allocation
q_gov.desc: What level of tag compliance and policy enforcement is in place in Azure?
q_gov.CRAWL: Tagging is optional or inconsistent (under 40% of resources carry Environment or CostCenter).
q_gov.WALK: Azure Policy requires mandatory tags on new resources, with over 80% compliance on the main ones.
q_gov.RUN: Tag compliance above 95% audited in CI/CD, a strict Management Group hierarchy, and automatic remediation of untagged resources.

q_auto.title: 5. FinOps Automation
q_auto.desc: What share of remediation and lifecycle actions run without manual intervention?
q_auto.CRAWL: Every action -- stopping VMs, changing SKUs, deleting orphaned disks -- is done by hand in the Azure portal.
q_auto.WALK: PowerShell and Azure CLI scripts, plus scheduled runbooks for routine maintenance.
q_auto.RUN: Infrastructure-as-code pipelines (Terraform/Bicep) with cost validation on pull requests and automatic remediation.

q_culture.title: 6. FinOps Culture & Organization
q_culture.desc: Is there a cross-functional team or a formal practice accountable for cloud cost?
q_culture.CRAWL: Cost is owned solely by finance or by traditional infrastructure.
q_culture.WALK: Engineering and Product can see their allocated cost and take part in monthly FinOps reviews.
q_culture.RUN: Unit-cost KPIs built into engineering team objectives, with a central FinOps enablement team.

Support.troubleshootingSubtitle: Common problems users run into during daily use, with their solution.
Support.troubleshootingDisclaimer: Before opening a ticket, please check this section — most questions are already answered here, and you'll resolve it without waiting on the support SLA.

troubleshooting_items.q: Costs on the Dashboard show $0 or don't appear
troubleshooting_items.a: Most often the daily sync hasn't run yet for your tenant (it runs once a day), or the Service Principal is missing the Cost Management Reader role on one or more subscriptions. Check Administration → Client Onboarding → "Verify Permissions" to confirm the Service Principal has every role required for your tier, on each subscription. If you just connected Azure, wait for the next daily sync before reporting this.

troubleshooting_items.q: I don't see my Azure subscription connected
troubleshooting_items.a: Confirm you ran the onboarding script (PowerShell) generated in Administration → Onboarding, in the correct subscription via Azure Cloud Shell. If you already ran it, it can take a few minutes to show up — reload the page. If it's still missing after a while, the app most likely needs Admin Consent granted in Azure AD.

troubleshooting_items.q: I can't edit my role or another user's permissions
troubleshooting_items.a: Only users with the Admin or Owner role can manage users and permissions. If you have the Reader or Collaborator role, ask an Admin/Owner in your organization to make the change, or to upgrade your role if appropriate.

troubleshooting_items.q: I'm not receiving notifications (Slack, Teams, or Email)
troubleshooting_items.a: Check Administration → Notification Channels to confirm the channel is enabled and that the master "Enable notifications" switch is also on — turning off the master switch disables every channel without deleting its configuration. Use each channel's "Test" button to confirm the integration actually works.

troubleshooting_items.q: I lost access to my authenticator app (2FA)
troubleshooting_items.a: Use one of the recovery codes saved when you enabled two-factor authentication (Security Settings → View Recovery Codes, if you saved them earlier). If you don't have them, you'll need support to verify your identity to disable 2FA on your account — open a ticket under the "Account" category.

troubleshooting_items.q: The AI Executive Report isn't generating or is very slow
troubleshooting_items.a: If your tenant uses the "System" (shared) provider, it can be subject to quota limits during peak hours. Configure your own API key in Administration → AI Configuration (BYOK) to avoid the shared limit and get faster responses. If the error persists with your own key, test the connection from that same screen.

troubleshooting_items.q: I can't create or edit a Cost Group
troubleshooting_items.a: Cost Groups is exclusive to Business and Enterprise plans, and requires the Admin or Owner role. Also, only Cost Groups you created manually with their own rule (by tag or Resource Group pattern) can be edited — groups auto-derived from the CostCenter tag don't have a rule of their own to edit.

troubleshooting_items.q: Single sign-on (SSO/SAML) isn't working for my organization
troubleshooting_items.a: SSO is configured jointly by your admin and CSCloudSolutions — if your organization hasn't finished that setup yet, you'll keep using standard Microsoft Entra ID login in the meantime. If it's already configured and failing, check with your identity team that the provider (Okta, Auth0, AD FS, etc.) is correctly connected in the WorkOS panel.

troubleshooting_items.q: The cost history has gaps or missing dates
troubleshooting_items.a: It's normal to see an occasional gap when Azure Cost Management returns temporary errors (throttling) during the daily sync — a backfill job runs every night and automatically fills in the last 2 months. If the gap is more than a few days old and hasn't filled in on its own, open a ticket.

troubleshooting_items.q: I can't invite more users / hit my plan's limit
troubleshooting_items.a: Each subscription tier has a user limit (Professional: 5, Business: 20, Enterprise: unlimited). If you need more users than your current plan allows, upgrade from Administration → Billing.

troubleshooting_items.q: The Dashboard is slow to load the first time
troubleshooting_items.a: The first load of the day can take longer because live data is being calculated against Azure (resource audit + cost projection). Subsequent loads are nearly instant since they're served from cache for 15 minutes. If it consistently takes more than 30 seconds, there may be a permissions issue on one of your subscriptions — check for a "degraded mode" banner if one appears.

RemediationModals.vm_burstableBody: B-Series (Burstable) instances accumulate CPU credits while the machine is idle and spend them during processing bursts. They are ideal for development or QA servers, or workloads averaging under 15% CPU. Changing the SKU requires restarting the virtual machine.
RemediationModals.vm_deallocTitle: Storage Cost Leak on Stopped VMs
RemediationModals.vm_deallocBody: In Azure, when a VM is in PowerState/deallocated, compute drops to $0.00, but the Managed Disks (OS Disk and Data Disks) keep billing at 100% of their monthly rate. Downgrading disks from Premium_LRS to Standard_LRS cuts the retention cost by over 65%.
RemediationModals.vm_bestPractice: 💡 FinOps Best Practice: Before deleting a deallocated virtual machine, take a managed Snapshot of the OS Disk. This preserves the machine's historical state for audit or fast restore at a fraction of the cost of keeping the disks provisioned.
RemediationModals.as_emptyPlanTitle: Safety Warning: Deleting an Empty Plan
RemediationModals.as_emptyPlanBody: This App Service Plan has no Web App or Function App attached (numberOfSites == 0). Deleting the resource is immediate and irreversible in Azure, freeing 100% of the recurring monthly bill.
RemediationModals.as_packingBody: Azure requirement: To move a Web App from one App Service Plan to another, both plans must live in the same Resource Group and the same geographic Region (Azure Webspace/Deployment Unit). If they are in different resource groups, the plan must be moved first or the configuration recreated.
RemediationModals.as_premiumBody: The Premium v3 (P0v3, P1v3) SKUs run on latest-generation Intel Xeon / AMD EPYC processors with ultra-fast NVMe SSD storage, and cost significantly less than the older Standard (S1/S2) or Premium v2 SKUs for the same amount of memory.
RemediationModals.as_governance: 💡 App Services FinOps governance: In Azure, cost comes from the App Service Plan (Workers and SKU) regardless of how many Web Apps are active. Consolidating multiple low-demand applications into one plan or reducing fixed workers maximizes density and drives down unit cost.
RemediationModals.fa_coldStartTitle: Architecture Consideration: Cold Starts vs. VNet
RemediationModals.fa_coldStartBody: The Consumption (Y1) plan scales to zero when it receives no traffic. The first executions after idling experience a Cold Start of ~500ms to 2s (depending on runtime). Also, the Consumption plan does not support traditional outbound private VNet integration (unless the new Flex Consumption plan is used).
RemediationModals.fa_telemetryBody: In Azure Functions, logs at Information or Verbose level without sampling often generate Application Insights bills larger than the compute itself. Setting samplingSettings.isEnabled = true in host.json reduces ingestion volume while preserving 100% of exception and error traces.
RemediationModals.fa_triggersBody: Queue and blob triggers poll the associated Storage Account constantly. Adjusting maxPollingInterval from 100ms to 2000ms drastically reduces billable read operations in Azure Storage with no perceptible impact on processing latency.
RemediationModals.fa_serverless: 💡 Serverless FinOps in Azure: Under the Consumption model, Azure grants 1 million free executions and 400,000 free GB-seconds per month per subscription. The biggest optimization opportunity is eliminating dedicated/premium plans for light workloads and controlling the associated storage and telemetry costs.

GovernanceHa.exemptedOk: {name} exempted from the high availability board
GovernanceHa.kpiCriticalTip: Production workloads at risk of data loss or full outage with no SLA. Registered exemptions do not count.
GovernanceHa.kpiHighTip: Production clusters and services on a single instance or zone.
GovernanceHa.kpiMediumTip: SKUs with no published SLA and non-redundant configurations on secondary workloads.
GovernanceHa.resilienceBanner: Resilience remediation: most of these recommendations require architectural changes — spreading across zones or enabling geo-redundancy means recreating the resource or picking a secondary region — so they are not a button. Only the public IP SKU migration and attaching a backup policy can be applied directly from the platform; the rest open a blueprint of the change for the team to run.
GovernanceHa.totalRemediationCost: Estimated cost of closing all active gaps: {amount}/mo.
GovernanceHa.emptyNoGaps: Azure Resource Graph reports no high availability gaps in the visible subscriptions.
GovernanceHa.emptyFiltered: No recommendation matches the applied filters.
GovernanceHa.noRegionReported: Region not reported by Resource Graph
GovernanceHa.backupRpoNote: A backup does not improve the availability SLA: it improves the RPO, that is, how much data is lost if something fails. That is why both figures match here.
GovernanceHa.listPriceDelta: This is a list-price delta, not a quote: the real amount depends on the region and on active commitments. Inter-zone traffic is billed separately.
GovernanceHa.apiRemediableNote: This fix is idempotent in ARM and can be applied from the platform. It is sent as a request to the Remediation Approvals flow, where a second operator reviews it before it touches Azure.
GovernanceHa.notApiRemediableNote: This gap cannot be closed via API: spreading across zones or attaching an Availability Set requires recreating the resource, and enabling geo-redundancy requires choosing the secondary region. The blueprint below describes the change so the infrastructure team can plan it.
GovernanceHa.cmdGeoRedundancy: # Requires choosing a secondary region and a failover window.
GovernanceHa.cmdAvailabilityZone: # Requires recreating the resource in a zone (it cannot be moved hot).
GovernanceHa.cmdAvailabilitySet: # An Availability Set can only be assigned when the VM is created.
GovernanceHa.exemptExplain: {name} stops counting in the KPIs but stays visible under the exempted filter. The justification is recorded against your user: someone will have to defend it at the next audit.
GovernanceHa.reasonPlaceholder: E.g. lab environment, recreated from a template in minutes.
GovernanceHa.costNote_BASIC_SKU_NO_SLA: Standard SKU charges ~$0.005/hour per static IP versus the Basic at no charge.
GovernanceHa.costNote_SINGLE_INSTANCE_CAPACITY: Doubles the App Service Plan cost: the delta equals the current instance's monthly rate.
GovernanceHa.costNote_NO_GEO_REDUNDANCY: A geo replica costs roughly the same as the primary instance.
GovernanceHa.costNote_NO_BACKUP: Recovery Services charges per protected instance plus the storage consumed.
GovernanceHa.costNote_NO_AVAILABILITY_ZONE: Spreading across zones has no compute charge, but inter-zone traffic is billed.
GovernanceHa.costNote_NO_AVAILABILITY_SET: An Availability Set has no cost of its own; it requires recreating the VM.
GovernanceHa.mockRisk_vm_payments_01: Production VM of the Payments API with no zone and no Availability Set: a zonal outage takes it completely out of service.
GovernanceHa.mockRisk_vm_payments_02: Second VM of the Payments cluster in the same implicit zone as the first: the redundancy is only apparent.
GovernanceHa.mockRisk_vm_db_prod_01: Self-hosted SQL Server with no backup policy in a Recovery Services Vault: undefined RPO.
GovernanceHa.mockRisk_sql_finance: Finance SQL with no failover group and no active geo replica.
GovernanceHa.mockRisk_vm_api_app_01: API tier on a single host with no Availability Set and no VMSS: Azure planned maintenance takes it down.
GovernanceHa.mockRisk_aks_prod_east: Production AKS with agent pools not spread across zones.
GovernanceHa.mockRisk_asp_portal_prod: Production App Service Plan with capacity 1: no single-instance SLA for PremiumV3.
GovernanceHa.mockRisk_cosmos_orders: Cosmos DB with a single write region configured.
GovernanceHa.mockRisk_pg_events: Flexible PostgreSQL with no Zone-Redundant high availability enabled.
GovernanceHa.mockRisk_pip_lb_front: Basic public IP: it does not support zones and Microsoft publishes no SLA for this SKU.
GovernanceHa.mockRisk_pip_vpn_gw: VPN Gateway public IP on the Basic SKU, on Azure's retirement path.
GovernanceHa.mockRisk_sql_app_prod: Application SQL with no geo-replication: local backup only.
GovernanceHa.mockRisk_asp_api_prod: API App Service Plan with capacity 1.
GovernanceHa.mockRisk_mysql_cms: Flexible MySQL with no HA enabled.
GovernanceHa.mockRisk_sapaymentlogs: Storage with LRS redundancy; ZRS would protect against a datacenter outage.
GovernanceHa.mockRisk_saarchive01: Archive on LRS: legal retention data with no geo-replication.
GovernanceHa.mockRisk_vm_test_bench: Benchmark VM with no Availability Set.
GovernanceHa.mockExempt_vm_test_bench: Lab environment: recreated from a template in minutes.
GovernanceHa.pageTooltip: Each gap shows the current and reachable SLA translated into monthly downtime minutes: ‘99.9%’ means nothing until you turn it into 43.8 minutes a month.
GovernanceHa.pageSubtitle: Detects virtual machines, databases and cloud resources with no zonal or geographic redundancy and no backup.

AutoBlockPolicies.tpl_vmSkus_desc: Lets you specify the list of virtual machine SKUs that can be deployed. Blocks provisioning of expensive families outside the list.
AutoBlockPolicies.tpl_vmSkus_rationale: Prevents an accidental GPU or M-series deployment from blowing up the month's bill.
AutoBlockPolicies.tpl_noPublicIp_name: Block public IPs on network interfaces
AutoBlockPolicies.tpl_noPublicIp_desc: Denies the creation of network interfaces with an associated public IP address. Meant for sandbox and testing subscriptions.
AutoBlockPolicies.tpl_noPublicIp_rationale: Every static public IP bills even with no traffic, and widens the exposure surface.
AutoBlockPolicies.tpl_inheritTag_name: Inherit a tag from the resource group
AutoBlockPolicies.tpl_inheritTag_desc: Adds or replaces the given tag with the parent resource group's value when a resource is created or updated.
AutoBlockPolicies.tpl_inheritTag_rationale: With no CostCenter on the resource, its spend has no owner and lands in no showback.
AutoBlockPolicies.tpl_requireCostCenter_name: Require the CostCenter tag on resources
AutoBlockPolicies.tpl_requireCostCenter_desc: Denies the creation of resources that do not carry the mandatory cost center tag.
AutoBlockPolicies.tpl_requireCostCenter_rationale: It is the preventive counterpart of inheritance: it keeps new unattributed spend from getting in.
AutoBlockPolicies.tpl_allowedRegions_desc: Limits the locations where resources can be deployed.
AutoBlockPolicies.tpl_allowedRegions_rationale: Unit price varies by region; deploying outside the approved ones raises cost with no warning.
AutoBlockPolicies.tpl_auditHttps_name: Audit storage accounts without secure transfer
AutoBlockPolicies.tpl_auditHttps_desc: Audits storage accounts that do not require HTTPS for data transfer.
AutoBlockPolicies.tpl_auditHttps_rationale: Audit does not block: it measures the gap before hardening to Deny.
AutoBlockPolicies.mockPolicy_deny_vm_skus_costosas_desc: Blocks the deployment of VM families outside the approved list (D, E and B series).
AutoBlockPolicies.mockPolicy_modify_heredar_costcenter_nam: Inherit CostCenter from the resource group
AutoBlockPolicies.mockPolicy_modify_heredar_costcenter_des: Adds the CostCenter tag with the parent RG's value when the resource does not carry it.
AutoBlockPolicies.mockPolicy_deny_ip_publica_sandbox_desc: Denies the creation of network interfaces with a public IP in the test subscriptions.
AutoBlockPolicies.mockPolicy_audit_storage_https_desc: Audits storage accounts that do not require HTTPS. It does not block: it measures the gap.
AutoBlockPolicies.mockPolicy_dine_diagnosticos_law_desc: Configures shipping diagnostic logs to the centralized workspace if it is not present.
AutoBlockPolicies.mockPolicy_deny_regiones_no_homologadas_: Limits deployment to eastus, westeurope and brazilsouth.
AutoBlockPolicies.mockPolicy_audit_tags_obligatorias_desc: Checks that every resource group declares Environment, Owner and CostCenter.
